prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live business listings from here, so I can’t give you an up‑to‑the‑minute list of Denver offices and phone numbers. I can, however, tell you exactly which specific types of practices to call, how to find the best ones in Denver fast, which questions to ask when you call, and why each type is worth contacting. If you want, tell me your ZIP code and I’ll show you the exact search queries and directories to get a short list of local offices right away.

Which offices to call (and why)
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS)
  - Why: OMSs are surgical specialists who handle complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts and implant placement under sedation or anesthesia. Best for medically complex cases, multiple implants, or if you need IV sedation.
- Periodontists
  - Why: Specialists in gums and bone who place implants and perform grafting. Often very experienced with implant site preparation and long‑term periodontal health.
- Prosthodontists (or restorative implant specialists)
  - Why: Prosthodontists focus on restoring implants (crowns, fixed bridges, full-arch prostheses). Call one when you need complex restorative planning or full-mouth implant prostheses.
- Multidisciplinary implant centers / private implant practices
  - Why: These centers coordinate surgeons + restorative dentists in‑house for same-day or streamlined treatment. Useful if you want a single point of contact and faster coordination.
- University dental clinics (University of Colorado School of Dental Medicine)
  - Why: Good for lower-cost treatment handled by residents under faculty supervision; often up‑to‑date technology and comprehensive care.

How to find specific Denver offices quickly
- Use these directories/searches:
  - AAOMS “Find a Surgeon” (oral surgeons)
  - American Academy of Periodontology “Find a Periodontist”
  - American College of Prosthodontists directory
  - American Academy of Implant Dentistry “Find a Dentist”
  - Google Maps + search terms: “dental implants Denver”, “oral surgeon Denver”, “periodontist Denver”
  - Read recent patient reviews on Google, Yelp, Healthgrades
- Look for practices that list: in‑office CBCT (3D imaging), Nobel/Biohorizons/ Straumann/Implant brand names, and restorative coordination.

Specific things to ask when you call (phone script)
- Do you place dental implants in your office? (If yes, ask how many per year.)
- Who will do the surgery, and who will do the final crown/restoration? Are both in the same office?
- Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging before treatment?
- Do you do bone grafting and sinus lifts if needed?
- What sedation options do you offer (local, oral sedation, IV)?
- Estimated total cost range for: (a) single implant + crown, (b) bone graft if needed, (c) full‑arch implant solutions — and whether the consultation has a fee.
- Warranty/guarantee and follow‑up schedule.
- Can you show before/after photos of similar cases and provide references or patient testimonials?
- Insurance/financing options and whether they accept my insurance.

How to prioritize the offices you call
1. Start with oral surgeons + periodontists (for surgical competence).
2. Call a prosthodontist or restorative dentist who performs implant restorations if your case needs esthetics/full‑arch work.
3. Add a university clinic if you want a lower‑cost option or a second opinion.
4. Contact one or two multidisciplinary implant centers for packaged pricing and convenience.

What to compare between providers
- Surgical experience (years, implants placed/year)
- Whether surgeon and restorative dentist coordinate closely
- Technology used (CBCT, guided surgery, implant brands)
- Sedation options and medical safety
- Cost breakdown and financing
- Reviews, before/after photos, and follow‑up care

Red flags to avoid
- Providers who won’t show photos of their work or can’t give a clear cost range.
- Practices that push a single implant brand as the only option without explanation.
- No CBCT or no clear plan for bone grafting or sinus issues when needed.
- Extremely low price with no explanation (could be inferior materials or inexperienced providers).

If you want, I can:
- Provide exact search queries and directories to get a short list of Denver offices near you.
- Draft a quick phone/email script you can use when contacting practices.
- Help evaluate 2–3 specific offices if you paste their names/quotes here.

Tell me your ZIP code or paste any practice names you found and I’ll help you next.
